title: The King's Peace (Excerpt)
author: Clerks of the Crown-Moot
pages: Of the King's Peace, the third roll. Whoso breaks the peace upon the Kingsway, within a league of a milestone, breaks it against the Crown itself and shall answer before the King's justice.
Blood-price: for a tooth, a shilling; for an eye, a mark; for a hand, three marks; for a life, the full wergild of the slain, paid to his kin and not to his lord. Unpaid blood-price becomes feud.
No one shall be hanged on rumour. The accused shall stand before Twelve Hands of neighbours, and the accuser also. Twelve Hands who swear falsely shall pay the wergild of the wronged.
Whoso defaces a grave, steals a grave-candle, or digs up the dead for any purpose shall be branded on the hand and put out of the parish. If the dead walk thereafter, he shall hang.
Every household fire pays one penny at Reaping, and the Flamekeeper's roll is witness. Who hides a hearth from the roll shall pay double, and the hearthkin will remember.
Mercenaries in the King's pay are bound by their contract and by the King's Peace. Should the King fail to pay, the fault is the King's, and he shall make it good before the company collects.
